DESCRIPTION
The Cincinnati Veterans Administration Medical Center (VAMC) has a requirement to provide Temporary Bulk Oxygen Rental & Support Services for Medical Gas Line Repair.
The intention of this Sources Sought is to obtain information only.  Please do not send a proposal.
Requested information: 
To aid acquisition planning, we re seeking capable and interested firms for the information requested. If your firm meets the criteria please send the point of contract (ronald.heidemann@va.gov) the following, via email:

1.  Contract Title.  Temporary Bulk Oxygen Rental & Support Services for Medical Gas Line Repair

2.  Background.  Provide a turnkey temporary bulk oxygen supply and services (rental tank, transport, installation, line hookup, controlled shutdown/bleeding, monitoring, and removal) to maintain uninterrupted oxygen service while VA performs a pin hole leak repair in the hospital s piped oxygen system. Work shall comply with VHA Directive 7515(1) and NFPA 99 Health Care Facilities Code requirements for medical gas systems 
3. Scope: The Contractor shall furnish all rental equipment, labor, materials, transport, and qualified personnel to:
Deliver and set a temporary bulk liquid oxygen (LOX) tank with vaporizers and regulators sized for hospital demand. 
Connect the temporary supply to the hospital oxygen pipeline (via EOSC/auxiliary connection or source valve), including gauges, check valves, and isolation devices; verify pressure, purity, and flow stability per NFPA 99 Chapter 5. 
Coordinate and execute a controlled shutdown and bleeding of affected lines, isolate zone valves, and validate alarm behavior with VA Clinical Engineering and Respiratory Therapy. 
Monitor supply, pressure, and alarms throughout the outage; maintain contingency oxygen cylinders for clinical areas at risk. 
Support VA repair team during line replacement/brazing and re-qualification (e.g., leak tests, purity checks, pressure verification), then transition back to the permanent bulk system and remove temporary equipment. 
4. Specific Tasks :  
Temporary LOX tank with vaporizers sized to meet peak hourly demand; provide pressure regulating, relief, and check devices; all oxygen service compatible, oil free. 

Auxiliary/EOSC connection hardware, hoses, and valves compliant with facility EOSC design; include filtration as required. (NFPA 99 2024 emphasizes auxiliary connections for emergency preparedness.) 

Alarm interface: ensure master and area alarms receive accurate signals during temporary supply (low pressure, source changeover).  

Performance. Delivery requirements are met:

Following VA repair and verification, transition back to primary bulk supply; execute valve re opening sequence, purge procedures, re pressurization, and alarm validation; document test results. 
Remove temporary equipment and restore site; submit as left drawings, pressure logs, and certification reports if applicable.
